source.text: Τοιγαροῦν καὶ ἡμεῖς, τοσοῦτον ἔχοντες περικείμενον ἡμῖν νέφος μαρτύρων, ὄγκον ἀποθέμενοι πάντα καὶ τὴν εὐπερίστατον ἁμαρτίαν, δι’ ὑπομονῆς τρέχωμεν τὸν προκείμενον ἡμῖν ἀγῶνα, ἀφορῶντες εἰς τὸν τῆς πίστεως ἀρχηγὸν καὶ τελειωτὴν Ἰησοῦν, ὃς ἀντὶ τῆς προκειμένης αὐτῷ χαρᾶς ὑπέμεινεν σταυρὸν αἰσχύνης καταφρονήσας, ἐν δεξιᾷ τε τοῦ θρόνου τοῦ θεοῦ κεκάθικεν.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore also we, so great having surrounding us a cloud of witnesses, weight having laid aside every and the easily-entangling sin, through endurance let us run the lying-before us race, \v 2 looking to the of the faith leader and perfecter Jesus, who for the lying-before him joy endured a cross, shame having despised, at [the] right hand and of the throne of the God has sat down.

en.L: Therefore we also, having so great a cloud of witnesses surrounding us, laying aside every weight and the sin that easily entangles, let us run through endurance the race lying before us, \v 2 looking to the pioneer and perfecter of the faith, Jesus, who for the joy lying before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} endured a cross, despising shame, and has sat down at [the] right hand of the throne of God.
en.B: So then, since we too have so vast a cloud of witnesses all around us, let us strip off every burden, and the sin that wraps itself around us so readily, and let us run the race laid out ahead of us, and run it with endurance. \v 2 Let us keep our eyes on Jesus, the pioneer who leads the way in faith and brings it to perfection. For the sake of the joy that lay ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} endured a cross and counted its shame as nothing, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has taken {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} seat at the right hand of God's throne.
en.R: So we too have a huge crowd of witnesses all around us. Their lives show us what faith looks like. So let us get rid of everything that slows us down, and the sin that so easily trips us up. Let us run with endurance the race that is in front of us. \v 2 Let us keep looking at Jesus. He leads the way in faith, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes faith complete. He knew the joy that was waiting for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} endured the cross. He did not care how shameful it was. And now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is seated in the place of honor, at the right hand of God's throne.

es.L: Por tanto, también nosotros, teniendo una nube tan grande de testigos que nos rodea, dejando a un lado todo peso y el pecado que fácilmente [nos] enreda, corramos mediante la perseverancia la carrera puesta delante de nosotros, \v 2 mirando al pionero y perfeccionador de la fe, Jesús, quien por la alegría puesta delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} soportó una cruz, despreciando [la] vergüenza, y se ha sentado a [la] derecha del trono de Dios.
es.B: Así pues, ya que también nosotros tenemos a nuestro alrededor una nube tan inmensa de testigos, quitémonos de encima toda carga y el pecado que con tanta facilidad se nos enrosca, y corramos la carrera trazada ante nosotros, y corrámosla con perseverancia. \v 2 Mantengamos los ojos en Jesús, el pionero que abre el camino en la fe y la lleva a su perfección. Por la alegría que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} esperaba, soportó una cruz y no hizo caso de su vergüenza, y ha tomado asiento a la derecha del trono de Dios.
es.R: Así que también nosotros tenemos a nuestro alrededor una enorme multitud de testigos. Sus vidas nos muestran cómo es la fe. Por eso, quitémonos de encima todo lo que nos hace ir más despacio, y el pecado que tan fácilmente nos hace tropezar. Corramos con perseverancia la carrera que está ante nosotros. \v 2 Sigamos mirando a Jesús. Él abre el camino en la fe, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hace que la fe sea completa. Sabía la alegría que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} esperaba, y por eso soportó la cruz. No {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} importó lo vergonzosa que era. Y ahora está sentado en el lugar de honor, a la derecha del trono de Dios.

decisions.choice: a cloud of witnesses: the great crowd of people of faith in chapter 11, whose lives bear witness
decisions.reason: μαρτύρων are people who testify. Chapter 11 has just said that the people of faith were "attested" or "commended" (11:2, 11:4, 11:5, 11:39, with the verb from the same family). A cloud was a common Greek picture for a vast throng. They surround the runners, but the stress falls on what their lives testify about faith more than on their watching.

decisions.choice: every weight: anything that burdens a runner and slows them down
decisions.reason: ὄγκον is bulk or weight. Runners stripped off whatever would hold them back. The author does not say what these weights are; they are set beside sin but are not simply the same thing.

decisions.choice: the sin that easily entangles: sin pictured as something that wraps around a runner
alternatives: the sin that is so readily admired
decisions.reason: εὐπερίστατον is found nowhere in Greek writing earlier than this verse, so its exact sense is uncertain. It is built from "well" and "stand around", and most likely describes something that readily surrounds and hampers, like a long robe around a runner's legs.

decisions.choice: run the race: the life of faith pictured as a footrace set out for us to finish
decisions.reason: ἀγῶνα is any contest; with the verb "run" it is a race. It is "lying before us", set out ahead for us to run. The same word "lying before" is used of Jesus' joy in verse 2.

decisions.choice: pioneer: the one who goes first, opening the way for others, and the one with whom it begins
decisions.reason: ἀρχηγὸν (also at 2:10, of Jesus as the pioneer of salvation) is one who starts something and leads others in it: a founder, a chief, one who goes ahead. Jesus has run the whole course of faith first, and opened it for others. The word also carries the idea of origin, so faith begins with him.

decisions.choice: perfecter: the one who brings faith to its goal (as at 2:10)
decisions.reason: τελειωτὴν is found nowhere in Greek before this verse. It comes from the verb τελειόω, which Hebrews uses for bringing someone or something to its intended goal (2:10; 5:9; 7:28; 11:40; 12:23). Jesus carried faith all the way through suffering to God's throne, and so brings it to completion in those who follow him (11:40).

decisions.choice: the faith: faith itself, which Jesus both began and completed
decisions.reason: The Greek says "the faith", with no "our". After chapter 11 it most likely means faith as such: the life of faith reaches its fullest form in Jesus. Adding "our" would narrow it to the readers' faith.

decisions.choice: for the sake of the joy ahead of him: the joy was the prize he looked toward
alternatives: instead of the joy he could have had
decisions.reason: ἀντὶ can mean "for, in return for" or "instead of". The joy is "lying before" him, as the race lies before the readers in verse 1, so it is most naturally the goal ahead, as a prize is ahead of a runner. The other reading takes the joy as something he gave up.

decisions.choice: the cross and its shame: crucifixion was the most shameful death in the Roman world
decisions.reason: Crucifixion was reserved for slaves and rebels and was meant to disgrace as well as kill. καταφρονήσας means to think little of something: Jesus treated the shame as nothing beside the joy. Deuteronomy 21:23 counts one hanged on a tree as cursed.

decisions.choice: sat down at the right hand of God's throne: Psalm 110:1, as in 1:3, 8:1 and 10:12
decisions.reason: The perfect tense (κεκάθικεν) means he sat down and remains seated. Hebrews builds much of its case on Psalm 110 (1:13; 5:6; 7:17). The right hand is the place of honor and shared rule.

decisions.choice: pioneer and perfecter (L); the pioneer who leads the way in faith and brings it to perfection (B); leads the way in faith and makes faith complete (R)
decisions.reason: "Pioneer" is the word used for the same noun at 2:10 (Literal and Balanced), so the link the author draws can be followed. Literal keeps the two nouns. Balanced and Readable say what Jesus does, so that the reader sees both his going first and his finishing. Readable says "complete" for this word family, as the book allows (see 2:10); Literal and Balanced keep the perfect family.

decisions.choice: cloud (L, B); crowd (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the picture of a cloud means: a huge crowd.

decisions.choice: Their lives show us what faith looks like
decisions.reason: Readable explains in what sense they are witnesses, following the meaning decision on the word.

decisions.choice: in the place of honor
decisions.reason: Readable explains what sitting at the right hand means.

decisions.choice: pionero y perfeccionador (L); el pionero que abre el camino en la fe y la lleva a su perfección (B); abre el camino en la fe y hace que la fe sea completa (R)
decisions.reason: "Pionero" is one who goes first and opens a way that others follow, the sense of m5, and it is the Spanish word for the same title at 2:10. "Perfeccionador" keeps the link with "perfeccionar", the letter's word for bringing to the goal (m6). Readable says both with verbs, as the English does.

decisions.choice: alegría
decisions.reason: "Alegría" is the everyday word for joy and is used for this word through Hebrews 12–13 (12:11, 13:17), so the joy set before Jesus and the joy the discipline later brings sound alike.

source.text: Ἀναλογίσασθε γὰρ τὸν τοιαύτην ὑπομεμενηκότα ὑπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν εἰς ἑαυτοὺς ἀντιλογίαν, ἵνα μὴ κάμητε ταῖς ψυχαῖς ὑμῶν ἐκλυόμενοι.

records.literal_gloss: Consider for the [one] such having endured by the sinners against themselves hostility, so that not you grow weary in the souls of you fainting.

en.L: For consider the [one] who has endured such hostility from sinners against themselves, so that you may not grow weary, fainting in your souls.
en.B: Weigh up what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} endured: such hostility from sinners, who were really working against themselves. Then you will not wear out and let your spirits give way.
en.R: Think about Jesus. Sinners fought against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with so much hate, and so they were really hurting themselves. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stood firm. Think about that, so that you will not get tired and give up.

es.L: Pues {{plural_you:consideren|considerad}} al que ha soportado tal hostilidad de parte de los pecadores contra sí mismos, para que no {{plural_you:se cansen|os canséis}}, desfalleciendo en {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} almas.
es.B: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} bien en lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} soportó: tanta hostilidad de parte de pecadores que en realidad actuaban contra sí mismos. Así no {{plural_you:se agotarán|os agotaréis}} ni {{plural_you:dejarán|dejaréis}} que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} ánimo se venga abajo.
es.R: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en Jesús. Los pecadores {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} atacaron con mucho odio, y así en realidad se hacían daño a sí mismos. Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se mantuvo firme. {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en eso, para que no {{plural_you:se cansen|os canséis}} ni {{plural_you:se rindan|os rindáis}}.

decisions.choice: against themselves (plural), as the SBLGNT reads
alternatives: against himself (singular): hostility directed at Jesus
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ. Several early witnesses read the plural ἑαυτοὺς, "against themselves": the sinners who opposed Jesus were acting against their own good (compare Numbers 16:38, 17:3 in Greek, where rebels are "sinners against their own lives"). Many others read the singular, "against him(self)", the easier reading. The SBLGNT text is followed here; reviewers must check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: consider: think carefully, weigh up, as one adds up an account
decisions.reason: Ἀναλογίσασθε means to reckon up or compare. The readers are to measure their own struggle against what Jesus went through (verse 4).

decisions.choice: grow weary, fainting in your souls: lose heart and give up inwardly
decisions.reason: Both verbs were used of runners who tire and collapse, continuing the picture of the race. ἐκλυόμενοι comes back in the quotation in verse 5 ("do not lose heart").

decisions.choice: Think about Jesus ... But he stood firm
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus, the one meant by "the one who endured", and says what enduring meant.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: As through Hebrews: every plural "you" (pronoun, possessive and verb form) is a reader setting, ustedes (the default) or vosotros.

source.text: οὔπω μέχρις αἵματος ἀντικατέστητε πρὸς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἀνταγωνιζόμενοι, καὶ ἐκλέλησθε τῆς παρακλήσεως, ἥτις ὑμῖν ὡς υἱοῖς διαλέγεται, Υἱέ μου, μὴ ὀλιγώρει παιδείας κυρίου, μηδὲ ἐκλύου ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐλεγχόμενος·

records.literal_gloss: Not yet unto blood have you resisted against the sin struggling, \v 5 and you have forgotten the exhortation which to you as to sons speaks: Son of me, not regard lightly [the] discipline of [the] Lord, nor faint by him being reproved;

en.L: You have not yet resisted to the point of blood in struggling against sin, \v 5 and you have forgotten the exhortation that speaks to you as to {{gender:children|sons}}: "My son, do not think lightly of [the] Lord's discipline, nor faint when you are reproved by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}};
en.B: Your fight against sin has not yet cost you your blood. \v 5 And you have forgotten the encouraging word that speaks to you as {{gender:children|sons}}: "My son, do not shrug off the Lord's discipline, and do not give way when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} corrects you.
en.R: You have struggled against sin, but you have not yet had to fight so hard that you were killed. \v 5 And you have forgotten the words that encourage you as God's {{gender:children|sons}}: "My child, when the Lord corrects you, do not treat it as unimportant. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shows you what you did wrong, do not give up.

es.L: Todavía no {{plural_you:han resistido|habéis resistido}} hasta [la] sangre luchando contra el pecado, \v 5 y {{plural_you:han olvidado|habéis olvidado}} la exhortación que {{plural_you:les|os}} habla como a hijos: «Hijo mío, no tengas en poco [la] disciplina del Señor, ni desfallezcas al ser reprendido por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}};
es.B: {{plural_you:Su|Vuestra}} lucha contra el pecado todavía no {{plural_you:les|os}} ha costado la sangre. \v 5 Y {{plural_you:han olvidado|habéis olvidado}} la palabra de aliento que se dirige a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} como a hijos: «Hijo mío, no tomes a la ligera la disciplina del Señor, y no te vengas abajo cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te corrija.
es.R: {{plural_you:Han luchado|Habéis luchado}} contra el pecado, pero todavía no {{plural_you:han tenido|habéis tenido}} que luchar tanto como para morir. \v 5 Y {{plural_you:han olvidado|habéis olvidado}} las palabras que {{plural_you:los|os}} animan como hijos de Dios: «Hijo mío, cuando el Señor te corrija, no lo trates como algo sin importancia. Cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te muestre lo que hiciste mal, no te rindas.

decisions.choice: to the point of blood: to the point of dying for the faith
decisions.reason: Resisting "unto blood" means struggling until one's blood is shed, as Jesus did (verse 2) and as some of the faithful in 11:35–37 did. The readers had suffered loss and prison (10:32–34) but not yet death.

decisions.choice: a statement: you have forgotten
decisions.reason: ἐκλέλησθε can be read as a statement or as a question. The SBLGNT punctuates it as a statement. Either way the author is reminding them of words they ought to know.

decisions.choice: Proverbs 3:11–12 (Greek), quoted through the end of verse 6
decisions.reason: The author quotes the Greek of Proverbs 3:11–12 and says it "speaks" (διαλέγεται) to the readers: Scripture still addresses them now, as in 3:7. In Proverbs a father teaches his son; the Lord's discipline is like a father's.

decisions.choice: "my son" speaks to every believer, men and women alike
decisions.reason: In Proverbs "my son" is the teacher's address to a pupil. The author applies it to all the readers as God's children ("as to sons", υἱοῖς). The singular stays because it is part of the quotation, and it means each believer.

decisions.choice: discipline: the training and correction a parent gives a child
decisions.reason: παιδείας is the whole upbringing of a child: teaching, training and correction. In verses 5–11 the author uses words from this family eight times. It is training for the child's good (verse 10), not punishment for its own sake.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God; the Hebrew of Proverbs 3:11 has the divine name YHWH
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament has κυρίου where the Hebrew of Proverbs has the name YHWH, and the author keeps it. The one who disciplines is God (verse 7).

decisions.choice: reproved: shown one's fault and corrected
decisions.reason: ἐλεγχόμενος means to bring a wrong into the open so that it can be put right.

decisions.choice: My child (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "my child" because the words are applied to every reader, as the meaning decision explains. Literal and Balanced keep "my son", the wording of the quotation.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The general plural takes in daughters as well as sons; "sons" is the alternative.

decisions.choice: exhortation (L); encouraging word (B); words that encourage (R)
decisions.reason: παρακλήσεως is both encouragement and earnest appeal. Literal keeps "exhortation"; Balanced and Readable say "encourage", as the book does elsewhere.

decisions.choice: fight so hard that you were killed
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom "to the point of blood".

decisions.choice: hijos, Hijo mío, no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English offers "children" with "sons" as the traditional form, and Readable says "My child". Spanish "hijos" already covers sons and daughters, and "Hijo mío" is the ordinary way a parent addresses a child, so, as with "hermanos", Spanish needs no setting; m4 says the address is to every believer.

decisions.choice: no tengas, no desfallezcas, te corrija: singular tú forms, no setting
decisions.reason: The proverb speaks to one son, so its verbs and pronouns are singular and take no ustedes / vosotros setting, while the author's own words around it stay plural.

source.text: ὃν γὰρ ἀγαπᾷ κύριος παιδεύει, μαστιγοῖ δὲ πάντα υἱὸν ὃν παραδέχεται.

records.literal_gloss: Whom for loves [the] Lord he disciplines, he scourges and every son whom he receives.

en.L: for whom [the] Lord loves {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} disciplines, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} scourges every son whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} receives."
en.B: Those whom the Lord loves, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} disciplines, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings the whip down on every son {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} takes as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own."
en.R: The Lord corrects those {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves. He even uses the whip on every child {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} welcomes as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own."

es.L: porque al que [el] Señor ama, disciplina, y azota a todo hijo que recibe».
es.B: El Señor disciplina a los que ama, y descarga el látigo sobre todo hijo que acepta como {{deity_pronoun:suyo|Suyo}}».
es.R: El Señor corrige a los que ama. Hasta usa el látigo con todo hijo que recibe como {{deity_pronoun:suyo|Suyo}}».

decisions.choice: Proverbs 3:12 (Greek), which differs from the Hebrew in its second line
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of Proverbs 3:12 reads "for whom the LORD (YHWH) loves he reproves, and as a father the son in whom he delights". The Greek translators read the same consonants as a verb, "and he causes pain", which gives "he whips every son he receives". The author quotes the Greek. Both lines compare the Lord to a father with his son.

decisions.choice: whips: a strong picture of hard correction
decisions.reason: μαστιγοῖ means to flog. In the household of the time, fathers corrected sons with the rod (Proverbs 13:24). The point is that hardship is a sign of being a son, not of being rejected.

decisions.choice: receives: accepts and acknowledges as his own son
decisions.reason: παραδέχεται is to welcome or acknowledge. A father in the Roman world formally received a child as his own.

decisions.choice: child (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "child", as it does with "my child" in verse 5.

source.text: εἰς παιδείαν ὑπομένετε· ὡς υἱοῖς ὑμῖν προσφέρεται ὁ θεός· τίς γὰρ υἱὸς ὃν οὐ παιδεύει πατήρ;

records.literal_gloss: For discipline you endure; as to sons to you is dealing the God; what for son [is there] whom not disciplines a father?

en.L: For discipline you are enduring; as with {{gender:children|sons}} God is dealing with you. For what {{gender:child|son}} [is there] whom a father does not discipline?
en.B: What you endure, you endure as discipline. God is dealing with you as {{gender:children|sons}}; and what {{gender:child|son}} is there that a father does not discipline?
en.R: The hard things you are going through are God's way of training you. They show that God is treating you as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{gender:children|sons}}. All fathers correct their children.

es.L: Para disciplina {{plural_you:están soportando|estáis soportando}}; como con hijos se porta Dios con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Porque ¿qué hijo [hay] a quien un padre no discipline?
es.B: Lo que {{plural_you:soportan|soportáis}}, lo {{plural_you:soportan|soportáis}} como disciplina. Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} trata como a hijos; ¿y qué hijo hay a quien su padre no discipline?
es.R: Las cosas difíciles que {{plural_you:están pasando|estáis pasando}} son la manera en que Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} entrena. Muestran que Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} trata como a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hijos. Todos los padres corrigen a sus hijos.

decisions.choice: a statement: it is for discipline that you endure
alternatives: a command: endure it as discipline
decisions.reason: ὑπομένετε has the same form as a statement and a command. As a statement it explains their sufferings; as a command it tells them how to bear them. The two come to much the same thing.

decisions.choice: "for discipline" (the SBLGNT reading)
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts read εἰς, "for, as". Some late ones read a word for "if", which is behind the King James Version's "If ye endure chastening". The SBLGNT text is followed; reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: every son was disciplined by his father
decisions.reason: In the ancient household it was taken for granted that a father trained and corrected his children. A son left uncorrected was a son neglected (verse 8).

decisions.choice: All fathers correct their children (R)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question, which expects the answer "none", into a plain statement.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}; {{gender:child|son}}
decisions.reason: The plural and the general "what son" include daughters; the traditional words are the alternative.

source.text: εἰ δὲ χωρίς ἐστε παιδείας ἧς μέτοχοι γεγόνασι πάντες, ἄρα νόθοι καὶ οὐχ υἱοί ἐστε.

records.literal_gloss: If but without you are discipline, of which sharers have become all, then illegitimate and not sons you are.

en.L: But if you are without discipline, of which all have become sharers, then you are illegitimate and not {{gender:children|sons}}.
en.B: If you go without the discipline that all {{gender:children|sons}} share in, then you are illegitimate, not true {{gender:children|sons}}.
en.R: Every true child is corrected. If God never corrected you, it would mean that you were not really {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{gender:children|sons}}. You would be like children whose father never accepted them as his own.

es.L: Pero si {{plural_you:están|estáis}} sin disciplina, de la cual todos han llegado a ser partícipes, entonces {{plural_you:son|sois}} ilegítimos y no hijos.
es.B: Si {{plural_you:se quedan|os quedáis}} sin la disciplina que todos los hijos comparten, entonces {{plural_you:son|sois}} ilegítimos, no hijos verdaderos.
es.R: Todo hijo verdadero es corregido. Si Dios nunca {{plural_you:los|os}} corrigiera, eso querría decir que en realidad no {{plural_you:son|sois}} {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hijos. {{plural_you:Serían|Seríais}} como hijos a quienes su padre nunca aceptó como suyos.

decisions.choice: illegitimate: children born outside a lawful marriage, with no claim on the father
decisions.reason: νόθοι are children born outside a lawful marriage. In Greek and Roman law they had no right to inherit, and the father had no duty to bring them up. Discipline is therefore the mark of a true heir.

decisions.choice: all: all true children of God
alternatives: the people of faith in chapter 11
decisions.reason: "All" are those who are sons, as the sentence goes on to say. It may also look back to the faithful of chapter 11, who all endured hardship.

decisions.choice: Every true child is corrected ... whose father never accepted them as his own
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the condition and explains what "illegitimate" meant for a child.

source.text: εἶτα τοὺς μὲν τῆς σαρκὸς ἡμῶν πατέρας εἴχομεν παιδευτὰς καὶ ἐνετρεπόμεθα· οὐ πολὺ μᾶλλον ὑποταγησόμεθα τῷ πατρὶ τῶν πνευμάτων καὶ ζήσομεν;

records.literal_gloss: Furthermore the indeed of the flesh of us fathers we had [as] correctors and we respected [them]; not much more shall we be subject to the Father of the spirits and shall live?

en.L: Furthermore, we had the fathers of our flesh as correctors, and we respected [them]; shall we not much more submit to the Father of spirits and live?
en.B: Again: our human fathers corrected us, and we held them in respect. Should we not much more put ourselves under the Father of spirits, and so live?
en.R: Think about it. Our fathers here on earth corrected us, and we respected them. So we should be even more willing to obey God, the Father of our spirits. Then we will truly live.

es.L: Además, tuvimos a los padres de nuestra carne como correctores, y [los] respetábamos; ¿no nos someteremos mucho más al Padre de los espíritus, y viviremos?
es.B: Además, nuestros padres humanos nos corregían, y los respetábamos. ¿No deberíamos someternos mucho más al Padre de los espíritus, y así vivir?
es.R: Pensémoslo bien. Nuestros padres aquí en la tierra nos corregían, y los respetábamos. Entonces deberíamos estar todavía más dispuestos a obedecer a Dios, el Padre de nuestros espíritus. Así viviremos de verdad.

decisions.choice: the fathers of our flesh: our human, earthly fathers
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means bodily human life. The fathers who gave us natural life are set against God, who is Father in another way.

decisions.choice: the Father of spirits: God, who gives and rules the life of the spirit
alternatives: the Father of spiritual beings, the angels
decisions.reason: Numbers 16:22 and 27:16 call God "the God of the spirits of all flesh". Set against "fathers of our flesh", the phrase most likely means God as the Father of our spirits, the source of our inner life.

decisions.choice: live: have true life with God
decisions.reason: ζήσομεν recalls Habakkuk 2:4, quoted at 10:38: "my righteous one will live by faith". Submitting to God's training leads to life, as refusing it leads to loss (verse 25).

decisions.choice: how much more: an argument from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: If we respected human fathers, there is far more reason to submit to God, as in 2:2–3 and 10:28–29.

decisions.choice: God, the Father of our spirits (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names God and adds "our", following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: Pensémoslo bien
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "Think about it." The verse speaks of "we" throughout, so Spanish uses "let us", which includes the author with his readers and needs no ustedes / vosotros setting.

source.text: οἱ μὲν γὰρ πρὸς ὀλίγας ἡμέρας κατὰ τὸ δοκοῦν αὐτοῖς ἐπαίδευον, ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὸ συμφέρον εἰς τὸ μεταλαβεῖν τῆς ἁγιότητος αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: They indeed for for few days according to the seeming good to them were disciplining, he but for the benefitting in order to share of the holiness of him.

en.L: For they disciplined [us] for a few days as seemed good to them, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [does so] for [our] benefit, so that [we] may share in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holiness.
en.B: Those fathers disciplined us for a short span of years, in whatever way seemed right to them. God does it for what truly benefits us, so that we may come to share in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holiness.
en.R: Our fathers corrected us for only a few years. They did what they thought was best. But God corrects us to help us, so that we can become holy, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is holy.

es.L: Porque ellos [nos] disciplinaban por pocos días según les parecía bien, pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} [lo hace] para [nuestro] provecho, para que participemos de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santidad.
es.B: Aquellos padres nos disciplinaron durante unos pocos años, del modo que les parecía mejor. Dios lo hace para lo que de verdad nos beneficia, para que lleguemos a participar de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santidad.
es.R: Nuestros padres nos corrigieron solo por unos pocos años. Hacían lo que les parecía mejor. Pero Dios nos corrige para ayudarnos, para que podamos llegar a ser santos, como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es santo.

decisions.choice: for a few days: for a short time, the years of childhood
decisions.reason: The phrase means a limited period, set against the lasting good God's discipline brings.

decisions.choice: as seemed good to them: by their own judgment, which could be wrong
decisions.reason: Human fathers did their best but could misjudge. God's discipline always aims at our real good.

decisions.choice: to share in his holiness: the goal of God's discipline is that his children become holy as he is
decisions.reason: ἁγιότητος is God's own holiness. Sharing it is the aim of the training, and it leads to verse 14: without holiness no one will see the Lord. Compare Leviticus 11:44, "be holy, for I am holy".

decisions.choice: God (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "he"; Balanced and Readable name God for clarity.

source.text: πᾶσα δὲ παιδεία πρὸς μὲν τὸ παρὸν οὐ δοκεῖ χαρᾶς εἶναι ἀλλὰ λύπης, ὕστερον δὲ καρπὸν εἰρηνικὸν τοῖς δι’ αὐτῆς γεγυμνασμένοις ἀποδίδωσιν δικαιοσύνης.

records.literal_gloss: All but discipline for indeed the present not seems of joy to be but of grief, later but fruit peaceable to those through it having been trained it yields of righteousness.

en.L: Now all discipline for the present does not seem to be [a matter] of joy but of grief, but later it yields [the] peaceable fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
en.B: At the time it is given, no discipline seems a matter for joy; it seems a matter for sorrow. But afterward it pays back those who have been trained by it with a harvest of peace: righteousness.
en.R: When we are being corrected, it does not feel like joy. It feels sad and painful. But later on, people who have been trained by it receive a reward. Their lives become righteous, and they have peace.

es.L: Ahora bien, toda disciplina, en el momento presente, no parece [cosa] de alegría sino de pesar; pero más tarde rinde [el] fruto pacífico de justicia a los que han sido entrenados por ella.
es.B: Mientras se recibe, ninguna disciplina parece motivo de alegría; parece motivo de dolor. Pero más adelante recompensa a quienes han sido entrenados por ella con una cosecha de paz: la justicia.
es.R: Cuando nos están corrigiendo, no sentimos alegría. Sentimos tristeza y dolor. Pero más adelante, los que han sido entrenados por la corrección reciben una recompensa. Sus vidas llegan a ser justas, y tienen paz.

decisions.choice: the peaceful fruit of righteousness: the fruit is righteousness, and it brings peace
alternatives: fruit that comes from being righteous
decisions.reason: The genitive δικαιοσύνης most likely says what the fruit is: a righteous life. "Peaceable" describes the fruit: after the struggle of training comes peace. Compare Isaiah 32:17 and James 3:18.

decisions.choice: trained: exercised, as an athlete is trained
decisions.reason: γεγυμνασμένοις is the verb behind the word "gymnasium". It continues the picture of the race in verse 1: hardship is training.

decisions.choice: yields: pays back, gives in return
decisions.reason: ἀποδίδωσιν is to give back what is owed. The pain of discipline is repaid later.

decisions.choice: a harvest of peace: righteousness (B); Their lives become righteous, and they have peace (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable unpack the compact phrase, following the meaning decision.

source.text: Διὸ τὰς παρειμένας χεῖρας καὶ τὰ παραλελυμένα γόνατα ἀνορθώσατε, καὶ τροχιὰς ὀρθὰς ποιεῖτε τοῖς ποσὶν ὑμῶν, ἵνα μὴ τὸ χωλὸν ἐκτραπῇ, ἰαθῇ δὲ μᾶλλον.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore the drooping hands and the weakened knees straighten, \v 13 and paths straight make for the feet of you, so that not the lame be put out of joint, be healed but rather.

en.L: Therefore straighten up the drooping hands and the weakened knees, \v 13 and make straight tracks for your feet, so that what is lame may not be turned out of joint, but rather be healed.
en.B: So raise your tired hands again and steady your shaking knees. \v 13 Make the tracks your feet walk on straight, so that the limb that is lame is not wrenched out of joint, but is healed instead.
en.R: So get your strength back! Lift up your tired arms, and make your weak knees strong again. \v 13 Walk on straight, level paths. Then a leg that is lame will not be twisted out of joint. Instead, it will heal.

es.L: Por tanto, {{plural_you:enderecen|enderezad}} las manos que cuelgan y las rodillas debilitadas, \v 13 y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} caminos rectos para {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pies, para que lo que está cojo no se descoyunte, sino más bien sea sanado.
es.B: Así que {{plural_you:levanten|levantad}} de nuevo {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} manos cansadas y {{plural_you:afirmen|afirmad}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} rodillas temblorosas. \v 13 {{plural_you:Tracen|Trazad}} rectas las sendas por donde andan {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pies, para que el miembro cojo no se tuerza y se disloque, sino que más bien se cure.
es.R: ¡Así que {{plural_you:recobren|recobrad}} las fuerzas! {{plural_you:Levanten|Levantad}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} brazos cansados, y {{plural_you:fortalezcan|fortaleced}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} rodillas débiles. \v 13 {{plural_you:Caminen|Caminad}} por sendas rectas y llanas. Así una pierna coja no se dislocará. Al contrario, se sanará.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 35:3 (Greek): strengthen weak hands and feeble knees
decisions.reason: Isaiah 35:3 calls on God's people to strengthen weak hands and feeble knees because God is coming to save them. The author uses the same picture for readers worn out by hardship.

decisions.choice: Proverbs 4:26 (Greek): make straight paths for your feet
decisions.reason: The wording follows the Greek of Proverbs 4:26 closely. A straight, level path lets an injured runner keep going without making the injury worse.

decisions.choice: put out of joint: dislocated
decisions.reason: ἐκτραπῇ can mean "turn aside", as from a road, or, as a medical term, "be dislocated". Set against "be healed", the medical sense fits best, though the picture of a path makes "turn aside" possible too.

decisions.choice: what is lame: whatever is weak, in each reader and in the community
alternatives: the weaker members of the church
decisions.reason: The neuter χωλὸν is "the lame part". Making the path straight helps the one who limps; the author may be thinking of weaker believers whom the others should help, as in verse 15.

source.text: Εἰρήνην διώκετε μετὰ πάντων, καὶ τὸν ἁγιασμόν, οὗ χωρὶς οὐδεὶς ὄψεται τὸν κύριον, ἐπισκοποῦντες μή τις ὑστερῶν ἀπὸ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ, μή τις ῥίζα πικρίας ἄνω φύουσα ἐνοχλῇ καὶ δι’ αὐτῆς μιανθῶσιν πολλοί, μή τις πόρνος ἢ βέβηλος ὡς Ἠσαῦ, ὃς ἀντὶ βρώσεως μιᾶς ἀπέδετο τὰ πρωτοτόκια ἑαυτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Peace pursue with all, and the holiness, which without no one will see the Lord, \v 15 watching lest anyone falling short from the grace of the God, lest any root of bitterness up springing should trouble and through it be defiled many, \v 16 lest any sexually immoral or profane as Esau, who for food one sold the birthright of himself.

en.L: Pursue peace with all, and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord, \v 15 watching lest anyone fall short of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness springing up cause trouble and through it many be defiled, \v 16 lest [there be] any sexually immoral or godless [person] like Esau, who for one meal sold his own birthright.
en.B: Seek peace with everyone, and go after holiness, since apart from it no one will see the Lord. \v 15 Watch over one another, so that none of you comes short of God's grace, no bitter root shoots up and causes trouble, defiling many through it, \v 16 and no one is sexually immoral or without regard for what is holy, as Esau was. He gave up his rights as the firstborn in exchange for one meal.
en.R: Work hard to live in peace with everyone. And work hard to be holy, because without holiness no one will see the Lord. \v 15 Watch out for each other. Make sure that no one turns away from God's grace. Do not let anyone become like a bitter root that grows up and causes trouble and makes many people unclean. \v 16 Do not let anyone be sexually immoral. And do not let anyone be like Esau, who did not care about what is holy. He sold his rights as the oldest son for just one meal.

es.L: {{plural_you:Persigan|Perseguid}} la paz con todos, y la santidad, sin la cual nadie verá al Señor, \v 15 cuidando de que nadie quede rezagado de la gracia de Dios, de que ninguna raíz de amargura, al brotar, cause perturbación y por medio de ella se contaminen muchos, \v 16 de que no [haya] nadie sexualmente inmoral o profano como Esaú, que a cambio de una única comida vendió su propia primogenitura.
es.B: {{plural_you:Busquen|Buscad}} la paz con todos, y {{plural_you:procuren|procurad}} la santidad, porque sin ella nadie verá al Señor. \v 15 {{plural_you:Velen|Velad}} unos por otros, para que ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} se quede lejos de la gracia de Dios, para que ninguna raíz amarga brote y cause problemas, contaminando a muchos, \v 16 y para que nadie sea sexualmente inmoral ni desprecie lo santo, como hizo Esaú. Él cedió sus derechos de primogénito a cambio de una sola comida.
es.R: {{plural_you:Esfuércense|Esforzaos}} por vivir en paz con todos. Y {{plural_you:esfuércense|esforzaos}} por ser santos, porque sin santidad nadie verá al Señor. \v 15 {{plural_you:Cuídense|Cuidaos}} unos a otros. {{plural_you:Asegúrense|Aseguraos}} de que nadie se aparte de la gracia de Dios. No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que nadie llegue a ser como una raíz amarga que crece, causa problemas y hace impuros a muchos. \v 16 No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que nadie sea sexualmente inmoral. Y no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que nadie sea como Esaú, a quien no le importaba lo que es santo. Vendió sus derechos de hijo mayor por una sola comida.

decisions.choice: pursue peace: Psalm 34:14 (33:15 Greek), "seek peace and pursue it"
decisions.reason: διώκετε means to chase after something with effort. The same pair of words, "peace" and "pursue", stands in Psalm 34:14 (quoted also in 1 Peter 3:11).

decisions.choice: holiness: being set apart for God and living accordingly
decisions.reason: ἁγιασμόν is the state and the life of one who belongs to God. Verse 10 has said that God's discipline aims at sharing his holiness. Here the readers are told to pursue it.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God, whom the pure in heart will see
alternatives: Christ, whom his people will see when he appears (9:28)
decisions.reason: Seeing God is the final hope of his people (Matthew 5:8; 1 John 3:2). Hebrews often calls Jesus "Lord" too (2:3; 7:14), so the words may refer to him.

decisions.choice: watching: taking care of one another
decisions.reason: ἐπισκοποῦντες is to oversee or look after. The whole community, not just the leaders, is to see that no one drops out.

decisions.choice: fall short of God's grace: fail to reach it, come too late for it
decisions.reason: ὑστερῶν is used in 4:1 of falling short of God's rest. Grace here is God's gift that has been offered in the gospel (compare 10:29).

decisions.choice: a root of bitterness: Deuteronomy 29:18 (29:17 Greek)
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy a "root" bearing bitter poison is a person among God's people who turns away to other gods and corrupts others. The word here for "cause trouble" is spelled almost exactly like the Greek of Deuteronomy's "in gall", and manuscripts of the Greek Deuteronomy have both.

decisions.choice: godless: having no regard for what is holy, treating it as common
decisions.reason: βέβηλος describes a person or thing that is not set apart for God. Esau treated his birthright, a gift with God's promise attached, as worth less than a meal.

decisions.choice: like Esau: certainly with "godless"; perhaps with "sexually immoral" as well
alternatives: Esau as an example of both
decisions.reason: Genesis does not call Esau sexually immoral, though he married foreign wives against his parents' wishes (Genesis 26:34–35), and later Jewish tradition painted him as immoral. The comparison holds at least for "godless", which his selling of the birthright shows.

decisions.choice: Esau sold his birthright: Genesis 25:29–34
decisions.reason: The firstborn's right was a double share of the inheritance and headship of the family (Deuteronomy 21:17), and in Abraham's family it carried God's promise. πρωτοτόκια recalls the "firstborn" enrolled in heaven in verse 23.

decisions.choice: Watch over one another (B); Watch out for each other (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "watching"; "one another" makes clear who watches over whom.

decisions.choice: birthright (L); rights as the firstborn (B); rights as the oldest son (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what a birthright was.

decisions.choice: profano (L); desprecie lo santo (B); no le importaba lo que es santo (R)
decisions.reason: "Profano" is one who treats what is holy as common, exactly the sense of m7; "impío" would say only that he was ungodly. Balanced and Readable say what the word means.

source.text: ἴστε γὰρ ὅτι καὶ μετέπειτα θέλων κληρονομῆσαι τὴν εὐλογίαν ἀπεδοκιμάσθη, μετανοίας γὰρ τόπον οὐχ εὗρεν, καίπερ μετὰ δακρύων ἐκζητήσας αὐτήν.

records.literal_gloss: You know for that even afterward wishing to inherit the blessing he was rejected, of repentance for place not he found, although with tears having sought out it.

en.L: For you know that even afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected; for he found no place of repentance, although he sought it out with tears.
en.B: You know that later, when he wanted to receive the blessing as his inheritance, he was turned away. He found no opening for repentance, even though he begged for it with tears.
en.R: You know what happened later. Esau wanted to receive his father's blessing, but he was turned away. He cried and searched hard, but he found no way for things to be changed back.

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que aun después, queriendo heredar la bendición, fue rechazado; pues no halló lugar de arrepentimiento, aunque con lágrimas la buscó insistentemente.
es.B: {{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} que más tarde, cuando quiso recibir la bendición como herencia, fue rechazado. No encontró ninguna posibilidad de arrepentimiento, aunque la suplicó con lágrimas.
es.R: {{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} lo que pasó después. Esaú quería recibir la bendición de su padre, pero fue rechazado. Lloró y buscó con mucho empeño, pero no encontró la manera de que las cosas volvieran a ser como antes.

decisions.choice: Esau's lost blessing: Genesis 27:30–40
decisions.reason: After Jacob had received Isaac's blessing, Esau begged his father for a blessing too, and wept aloud (Genesis 27:34, 38). ἀπεδοκιμάσθη means rejected after testing, turned away as unfit.

decisions.choice: no place for repentance: no way for what had been done to be undone
alternatives: Esau could not bring himself to a real change of heart
Isaac could not change his mind and take back the blessing (Genesis 27:33)
decisions.reason: μετανοίας means a change of mind. The author does not say whose. It may be Esau's own, which came too late to undo the sale; or Isaac's, who would not take back the blessing he had given Jacob: "I have blessed him; yes, and he will be blessed" (Genesis 27:33). Either way, Esau's tears could not reverse it. Hebrews 6:4–6 gives a similar warning.

decisions.choice: it: the blessing, or the repentance
decisions.reason: αὐτήν is feminine, and so are both "blessing" and "repentance" in Greek. Genesis has Esau weeping for the blessing; the nearer word is "repentance".

decisions.choice: his father's blessing (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says whose blessing it was (Isaac's, Genesis 27).

decisions.choice: la buscó (L); la suplicó (B), with "la" left open
decisions.reason: Spanish "la" can point back to "la bendición" or to the repentance ("arrepentimiento" in L, "posibilidad" in B), so the question in m3 stays open as it does in the Greek.

source.text: Οὐ γὰρ προσεληλύθατε ψηλαφωμένῳ καὶ κεκαυμένῳ πυρὶ καὶ γνόφῳ καὶ ζόφῳ καὶ θυέλλῃ καὶ σάλπιγγος ἤχῳ καὶ φωνῇ ῥημάτων, ἧς οἱ ἀκούσαντες παρῃτήσαντο μὴ προστεθῆναι αὐτοῖς λόγον·

records.literal_gloss: Not for you have approached [what is] being touched and having been kindled with fire and to darkness and to gloom and to storm, \v 19 and of a trumpet to sound and to a voice of words, which those having heard begged not to be added to them a word;

en.L: For you have not approached [something] that can be touched, and a blazing fire, and darkness and gloom and whirlwind, \v 19 and [the] sound of a trumpet and a voice of words, which those who heard begged that no further word be spoken to them;
en.B: You have not approached a mountain that could be touched, ablaze with fire, nor darkness and gloom and storm, \v 19 nor the blast of a trumpet and a voice speaking, so that those who heard it begged not to be spoken to anymore.
en.R: You have not come near to a mountain that you can touch, as the people of Israel did at Mount Sinai. That mountain was burning with fire. It was covered with darkness and gloom and storm. \v 19 A trumpet blasted, and a voice spoke words. The people who heard that voice begged that it would not say anything more to them.

es.L: Porque no {{plural_you:se han acercado|os habéis acercado}} a [algo] que se puede tocar, y a un fuego ardiente, y a oscuridad y tinieblas y torbellino, \v 19 y a [un] sonido de trompeta y a una voz de palabras, la cual los que [la] oyeron rogaron que no se les hablara ninguna palabra más;
es.B: No {{plural_you:se han acercado|os habéis acercado}} a un monte que se podía tocar, envuelto en llamas, ni a la oscuridad, las tinieblas y la tormenta, \v 19 ni al toque de trompeta y a una voz que hablaba, de modo que los que la oyeron suplicaron que no se les hablara más.
es.R: No {{plural_you:se han acercado|os habéis acercado}} a un monte que se puede tocar, como hizo el pueblo de Israel en el monte Sinaí. Aquel monte ardía en fuego. Estaba cubierto de oscuridad, de tinieblas y de tormenta. \v 19 Sonó una trompeta, y una voz pronunció palabras. La gente que oyó esa voz suplicó que no les dijera nada más.

decisions.choice: Sinai, where God gave the law: Exodus 19:16–19; 20:18–19; Deuteronomy 4:11–12; 5:22–27
decisions.reason: The author does not name the mountain but describes it in the words of Exodus and Deuteronomy: fire, darkness, gloom, storm, trumpet and voice (Deuteronomy 4:11; 5:22). The people begged that God would not speak to them directly (Exodus 20:19; Deuteronomy 5:25–27; 18:16).

decisions.choice: no word for "mountain" after "touched"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add ὄρει, "mountain", after "touched", as the King James Version has it; the earliest manuscripts do not. The SBLGNT has no noun here, which sharpens the contrast with "Mount Zion" in verse 22. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: two things: something that can be touched, and a blazing fire
alternatives: one thing: a fire that could be touched and was blazing
decisions.reason: The two participles may both describe πυρὶ, "fire", or the first may stand alone for the touchable mountain. Since the point is that Sinai was physical and earthly, set against the heavenly Zion, the first most likely stands alone.

decisions.choice: approached: come near to God, as worshipers do
decisions.reason: προσεληλύθατε is the word Hebrews uses for drawing near to God in worship (4:16; 7:25; 10:22). The perfect tense says where the readers now stand. It comes back in verse 22.

decisions.choice: a mountain (B); a mountain ... Mount Sinai (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the mountain that the whole passage describes (verse 20); Readable names it. Literal follows the SBLGNT, which has no noun.

decisions.choice: approached (L, B); come near (R)
decisions.reason: The book's word for drawing near to God.

source.text: οὐκ ἔφερον γὰρ τὸ διαστελλόμενον· Κἂν θηρίον θίγῃ τοῦ ὄρους, λιθοβοληθήσεται·

records.literal_gloss: not they could bear for the being commanded: If even a beast touches the mountain, it will be stoned;

en.L: for they could not bear what was commanded: "If even a wild animal touches the mountain, it will be stoned."
en.B: The order was more than they could bear: "Even an animal that touches the mountain must be stoned."
en.R: They could not stand to hear the command God gave: "If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be killed with stones."

es.L: porque no podían soportar lo que se ordenaba: «Si aun un animal salvaje toca el monte, será apedreado».
es.B: La orden era más de lo que podían soportar: «Aun el animal que toque el monte debe ser apedreado».
es.R: No soportaban oír la orden que Dios dio: «Si aun un animal toca el monte, hay que matarlo a pedradas».

decisions.choice: Exodus 19:12–13, given in the author's own short form
decisions.reason: God ordered that no person or animal touch the mountain while he was present on it; whoever did must be put to death by stoning or arrows, so that no one else would touch them (Exodus 19:12–13). The mountain was made holy by God's presence.

decisions.choice: the command ends with "it will be stoned"
alternatives: adds "or shot down with an arrow"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "or shot through with an arrow" from Exodus 19:13, as the King James Version has it. The earliest manuscripts and the SBLGNT do not. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the command God gave (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says who gave the command.

source.text: καί, οὕτω φοβερὸν ἦν τὸ φανταζόμενον, Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν· Ἔκφοβός εἰμι καὶ ἔντρομος.

records.literal_gloss: And so fearful was the appearing [thing], Moses said: Terrified I am and trembling.

en.L: And so terrifying was the sight [that] Moses said, "I am terrified and trembling."
en.B: What appeared was so fearsome that Moses said, "I am full of dread, and I am shaking."
en.R: What the people saw was so frightening that even Moses said, "I am terrified, and I am shaking."

es.L: Y tan temible era la visión, [que] Moisés dijo: «Estoy aterrado y tembloroso».
es.B: Lo que se mostró era tan espantoso que Moisés dijo: «Estoy lleno de pavor, y estoy temblando».
es.R: Lo que la gente vio daba tanto miedo que hasta Moisés dijo: «Estoy aterrado, y estoy temblando».

decisions.choice: Moses' words: Deuteronomy 9:19 (Greek)
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy 9:19 Moses says "I was terrified" (Ἔκφοβός) of the Lord's anger after the golden calf. Exodus 19:16 says the people trembled at Sinai. The author joins the two to show that even Moses, who spoke with God face to face, was afraid.

decisions.choice: the sight: what appeared, the visible display
decisions.reason: φανταζόμενον is what was shown or seen: the fire, cloud and darkness on the mountain.

decisions.choice: even Moses (R)
decisions.reason: Readable brings out the point that even Moses was afraid.

source.text: ἀλλὰ προσεληλύθατε Σιὼν ὄρει καὶ πόλει θεοῦ ζῶντος, Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἐπουρανίῳ, καὶ μυριάσιν ἀγγέλων, πανηγύρει καὶ ἐκκλησίᾳ πρωτοτόκων ἀπογεγραμμένων ἐν οὐρανοῖς, καὶ κριτῇ θεῷ πάντων, καὶ πνεύμασι δικαίων τετελειωμένων, καὶ διαθήκης νέας μεσίτῃ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ αἵματι ῥαντισμοῦ κρεῖττον λαλοῦντι παρὰ τὸν Ἅβελ.

records.literal_gloss: But you have approached Zion Mount and city of God living, Jerusalem heavenly, and to myriads of angels, to festal gathering \v 23 and to assembly of firstborn having been enrolled in heavens, and to judge God of all, and to spirits of righteous having been made perfect, \v 24 and of covenant new mediator Jesus, and to blood of sprinkling better speaking than the Abel.

en.L: But you have approached Mount Zion and [the] city of [the] living God, [the] heavenly Jerusalem, and myriads of angels, a festal gathering \v 23 and assembly of [the] firstborn who are enrolled in [the] heavens, and a judge [who is] God of all, and [the] spirits of righteous [people] made perfect, \v 24 and Jesus, mediator of a new covenant, and [the] blood of sprinkling that speaks better than Abel.
en.B: No: you have approached Mount Zion, the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. You have approached myriads of angels, a festival gathering \v 23 and assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven. You have approached a judge who is God of all, and the spirits of righteous people who have been made perfect, \v 24 and Jesus, mediator of a new covenant, and blood sprinkled for cleansing, which says something better than Abel said.
en.R: Instead, you have come near to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God. It is the Jerusalem that is in heaven. You have come near to thousands and thousands of angels. You have come to a joyful festival \v 23 where God's people are gathered, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} firstborn children, whose names are written in heaven. You have come to God, who is the judge of everyone. You have come to the spirits of righteous people whom God has made complete. \v 24 You have come to Jesus, who brings people into a new covenant with God. And you have come to the blood of Jesus that was sprinkled. It says something better than Abel said.

es.L: Sino que {{plural_you:se han acercado|os habéis acercado}} al monte Sion y a [la] ciudad del Dios vivo, [la] Jerusalén celestial, y a miríadas de ángeles, a una reunión festiva \v 23 y asamblea de [los] primogénitos inscritos en [los] cielos, y a un juez [que es] Dios de todos, y a [los] espíritus de justos hechos perfectos, \v 24 y a Jesús, mediador de un nuevo pacto, y a [la] sangre de aspersión que habla mejor que Abel.
es.B: Al contrario, {{plural_you:se han acercado|os habéis acercado}} al monte Sion, la ciudad del Dios vivo, la Jerusalén celestial. {{plural_you:Se han acercado|Os habéis acercado}} a miríadas de ángeles, a una reunión festiva \v 23 y asamblea de los primogénitos inscritos en el cielo. {{plural_you:Se han acercado|Os habéis acercado}} a un juez que es Dios de todos, y a los espíritus de los justos que han sido hechos perfectos, \v 24 y a Jesús, mediador de un nuevo pacto, y a la sangre rociada para purificar, que dice algo mejor que lo que dijo Abel.
es.R: En cambio, {{plural_you:ustedes se han acercado|vosotros os habéis acercado}} al monte Sion, a la ciudad del Dios vivo. Es la Jerusalén que está en el cielo. {{plural_you:Se han acercado|Os habéis acercado}} a miles y miles de ángeles. {{plural_you:Han llegado|Habéis llegado}} a una fiesta llena de alegría, \v 23 donde está reunido el pueblo de Dios, {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hijos primogénitos, cuyos nombres están escritos en el cielo. {{plural_you:Han llegado|Habéis llegado}} a Dios, que es el juez de todos. {{plural_you:Han llegado|Habéis llegado}} a los espíritus de los justos a quienes Dios ha hecho completos. \v 24 {{plural_you:Han llegado|Habéis llegado}} a Jesús, que lleva a las personas a un nuevo pacto con Dios. Y {{plural_you:han llegado|habéis llegado}} a la sangre de Jesús, que fue rociada. Esa sangre dice algo mejor que lo que dijo Abel.

decisions.choice: Mount Zion, the heavenly Jerusalem: the city of God where his people now draw near
decisions.reason: Zion was the hill of Jerusalem where God's temple stood (Psalm 48:1–2). The author means the true city above, the one Abraham looked for (11:10, 11:16) and the readers seek (13:14); compare Galatians 4:26 and Revelation 21:2. Believers have already come to it in worship, though they still wait to enter it fully.

decisions.choice: a festal gathering together with the assembly of the firstborn, as the SBLGNT punctuates
alternatives: myriads of angels in festal gathering
decisions.reason: πανηγύρει is a joyful festival assembly. The SBLGNT places a comma after "angels", so the festival goes with the assembly of the firstborn in verse 23. Other editions take it with the angels. Both readings speak of a joyful gathering in heaven.

decisions.choice: assembly: the gathered people of God (as at 2:12)
decisions.reason: ἐκκλησίᾳ is an assembly of people called together. Here it is the whole people of God, gathered around God in heaven.

decisions.choice: the firstborn enrolled in heaven: God's people, heirs with the firstborn's rights
decisions.reason: πρωτοτόκων is plural: all God's people. In Exodus 4:22 Israel is God's firstborn son, and the firstborn received the inheritance; the word answers Esau, who sold his birthright (verse 16). They are enrolled in heaven like citizens on a city's register (Luke 10:20).

decisions.choice: a judge who is God of all
decisions.reason: The Greek order is "a judge, God of all". Either way God is the judge before whom all stand, which gives weight to the warning in verse 25.

decisions.choice: the spirits of righteous people made perfect: the faithful who have died, now brought to their goal
decisions.reason: These are the righteous dead, such as the faithful of chapter 11, who "would not be made perfect apart from us" (11:40). Through Christ they have now reached the goal (as at 2:10).

decisions.choice: mediator of a new covenant: the one through whom the new covenant of Jeremiah 31 is made
decisions.reason: μεσίτῃ is a go-between who brings two parties into agreement (8:6; 9:15). The word for "new" here differs from the one in 8:8, 8:13 and 9:15, with little difference in sense.

decisions.choice: sprinkled blood that speaks better than Abel: Exodus 24:8; Genesis 4:10
decisions.reason: Moses sprinkled blood to seal the covenant (Exodus 24:8; Hebrews 9:19–22). Abel's blood cried out from the ground (Genesis 4:10), and through his faith "he still speaks" (11:4). Jesus' blood speaks a better word: cleansing and forgiveness rather than a cry for justice. The Greek says "than Abel", which may mean Abel himself or his blood.

decisions.choice: You have approached ... (B); You have come ... (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has the verb once and lists everything that follows. Balanced and Readable repeat it to break up the long list.

decisions.choice: made perfect (L, B); made complete (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "complete" for the perfect word family, as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: who brings people into a new covenant with God; the blood of Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word "mediator" and says whose blood is meant.

source.text: Βλέπετε μὴ παραιτήσησθε τὸν λαλοῦντα· εἰ γὰρ ἐκεῖνοι οὐκ ἐξέφυγον ἐπὶ γῆς παραιτησάμενοι τὸν χρηματίζοντα, πολὺ μᾶλλον ἡμεῖς οἱ τὸν ἀπ’ οὐρανῶν ἀποστρεφόμενοι·

records.literal_gloss: See not you refuse the [one] speaking; if for those not escaped on earth having refused the [one] warning, much more we the [one] from heavens turning away from;

en.L: See that you do not refuse the one who is speaking. For if those did not escape when they refused the one who warned [them] on earth, much less [will] we [escape] who turn away from the one [who warns] from [the] heavens;
en.B: Be careful not to refuse the one who is speaking to you. They rejected the one who warned them on earth, and they did not escape. Far less will we escape if we turn our backs on the one who warns us from heaven.
en.R: Be careful! Do not refuse to listen to God, who is speaking to you. The people of Israel refused to listen when God warned them here on earth, and they did not escape punishment. So we will surely not escape if we turn away from God, who warns us from heaven.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} que no {{plural_you:rechacen|rechacéis}} al que habla. Porque si aquellos no escaparon cuando rechazaron al que [les] advertía en [la] tierra, mucho menos [escaparemos] nosotros, los que nos apartamos del que [advierte] desde [los] cielos;
es.B: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado de no rechazar al que {{plural_you:les|os}} habla. Ellos rechazaron al que les advertía en la tierra, y no escaparon. Mucho menos escaparemos nosotros si damos la espalda al que nos advierte desde el cielo.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado! No {{plural_you:se nieguen|os neguéis}} a escuchar a Dios, que {{plural_you:les|os}} está hablando. El pueblo de Israel no quiso escuchar cuando Dios les advirtió aquí en la tierra, y no escaparon del castigo. Así que nosotros de ningún modo escaparemos si nos apartamos de Dios, que nos advierte desde el cielo.

decisions.choice: the one speaking is God, who spoke on earth at Sinai and now speaks from heaven
alternatives: Moses warned them on earth, and Christ warns from heaven
decisions.reason: Verse 26 says it was "his voice" that shook the earth then, which was God at Sinai. God has now spoken in his Son (1:1–2), and the sprinkled blood "speaks" (verse 24). Some take the one on earth as Moses, who passed on God's words.

decisions.choice: warned: gave a message from God
decisions.reason: χρηματίζοντα is used for God giving a warning or instruction (8:5; 11:7).

decisions.choice: much more: an argument from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: Literally "much more [shall] we [not escape]". As in 2:2–3 and 10:28–29, if those who rejected the earthly warning were punished, rejecting the warning from heaven is more serious still.

decisions.choice: God; the people of Israel (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker and the people, following the meaning decision.

source.text: οὗ ἡ φωνὴ τὴν γῆν ἐσάλευσεν τότε, νῦν δὲ ἐπήγγελται λέγων· Ἔτι ἅπαξ ἐγὼ σείσω οὐ μόνον τὴν γῆν ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν οὐρανόν.

records.literal_gloss: whose the voice the earth shook then, now but he has promised saying: Yet once I will shake not only the earth but also the heaven.

en.L: whose voice shook the earth then, but now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has promised, saying, "Yet once [more] I will shake not only the earth but also heaven."
en.B: At that time {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice shook the earth, but now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made a promise: "One more time I will shake not the earth alone, but heaven as well."
en.R: When God spoke at Mount Sinai, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice made the earth shake. But now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has promised, "One more time I will shake not just the earth, but heaven too."

es.L: cuya voz sacudió entonces la tierra, pero ahora ha prometido, diciendo: «Todavía una vez [más] sacudiré no solo la tierra, sino también el cielo».
es.B: En aquel tiempo {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voz hizo temblar la tierra, pero ahora ha hecho una promesa: «Una vez más haré temblar no la tierra sola, sino el cielo también».
es.R: Cuando Dios habló en el monte Sinaí, {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voz hizo temblar la tierra. Pero ahora ha prometido: «Una vez más haré temblar no solo la tierra, sino también el cielo».

decisions.choice: Haggai 2:6 (Greek)
decisions.reason: God promises through Haggai to shake heaven and earth, sea and dry land, once more, before he fills his house with glory. The author quotes it in short form and arranges it "not only ... but also" to put the weight on heaven. The earth shook when God came down on Sinai (Exodus 19:18; Psalm 68:8).

decisions.choice: yet once more: one more time, a final shaking
decisions.reason: ἅπαξ means "once", with the sense "once for all". Verse 27 draws out that this shaking is final.

decisions.choice: When God spoke at Mount Sinai (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says whose voice and when.

decisions.choice: ha prometido, with no deity_pronoun
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves the subject pronoun out where the verb shows who acts, so the English "he has promised" has no separate pronoun to carry the setting. A pronoun for God or Christ takes the setting wherever Spanish writes one.

source.text: τὸ δὲ Ἔτι ἅπαξ δηλοῖ τῶν σαλευομένων μετάθεσιν ὡς πεποιημένων, ἵνα μείνῃ τὰ μὴ σαλευόμενα.

records.literal_gloss: The now Yet once signifies of the being shaken removal as of having been made, so that may remain the not being shaken.

en.L: Now this "Yet once [more]" makes clear the removal of the things being shaken, as of things that have been made, so that the things not being shaken may remain.
en.B: That phrase, "one more time," makes clear that whatever is shaken will be removed, since it belongs to what was made, so that what is not shaken will remain.
en.R: The words "one more time" show that God will remove everything that can be shaken, the things that were made. Then only the things that cannot be shaken will be left.

es.L: Y este «Todavía una vez [más]» indica la remoción de las cosas que son sacudidas, como de cosas que han sido hechas, para que permanezcan las cosas que no son sacudidas.
es.B: Esa frase, «una vez más», deja claro que lo que es sacudido será quitado, porque pertenece a lo que fue hecho, para que permanezca lo que no es sacudido.
es.R: Las palabras «una vez más» muestran que Dios quitará todo lo que se puede sacudir, las cosas que fueron hechas. Entonces solo quedarán las cosas que no se pueden sacudir.

decisions.choice: removal: taking away
decisions.reason: μετάθεσιν can mean removal or change. It is used of the change of the law in 7:12, and its verb of Enoch being taken up in 11:5. The author may mean that the created order is removed, or that it is changed; either way, only the unshakable remains.

decisions.choice: as things that have been made: created things, which can pass away
decisions.reason: Being made, they are not lasting in themselves. Hebrews 1:10–12 (Psalm 102:25–27) has already said that earth and heavens will perish and be changed like clothing, while the Son remains.

decisions.choice: remain: last for ever
decisions.reason: μείνῃ is the verb of lasting. Hebrews uses it for the Son (1:11), for what believers possess (10:34) and, in the next chapter, for love (13:1) and the city to come (13:14).

source.text: διὸ βασιλείαν ἀσάλευτον παραλαμβάνοντες ἔχωμεν χάριν, δι’ ἧς λατρεύωμεν εὐαρέστως τῷ θεῷ μετὰ εὐλαβείας καὶ δέους, καὶ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν πῦρ καταναλίσκον.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore a kingdom unshakable receiving let us have gratitude, through which let us serve well-pleasingly the God with reverence and awe; \v 29 also for the God of us [is] a fire consuming.

en.L: Therefore, receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us have gratitude, through which we may serve God in a pleasing way, with reverence and awe; \v 29 for indeed our God [is] a consuming fire.
en.B: So, as people who are being given a kingdom that nothing can shake, let us hold on to gratitude, and through it serve God in a way that pleases {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, with reverence and awe. \v 29 For our God really is a consuming fire.
en.R: We are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken. So let us be thankful. Let us worship God in a way that pleases {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, with deep respect and awe. \v 29 For our God is a fire that burns things up completely.

es.L: Por tanto, recibiendo un reino que no puede ser sacudido, tengamos gratitud, con la cual sirvamos a Dios de manera agradable, con reverencia y temor; \v 29 porque nuestro Dios, en efecto, [es] un fuego que consume.
es.B: Así pues, como quienes están recibiendo un reino que nada puede sacudir, aferrémonos a la gratitud, y por medio de ella sirvamos a Dios de un modo que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} agrade, con reverencia y temor. \v 29 Porque nuestro Dios es de verdad un fuego que consume.
es.R: Estamos recibiendo un reino que no puede ser sacudido. Por eso, seamos agradecidos. Adoremos a Dios de una manera que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} agrade, con profundo respeto y temor. \v 29 Porque nuestro Dios es un fuego que lo quema todo por completo.

decisions.choice: let us be thankful: the idiom "have grace" means to give thanks
alternatives: let us hold on to grace
decisions.reason: χάριν is usually "grace", God's free gift. With the verb "have" it is a common Greek way of saying "thanks" (Luke 17:9; 1 Timothy 1:12; 2 Timothy 1:3). The gift of a kingdom is answered with gratitude. Some take it as "let us hold on to grace", which also fits the letter (13:9).

decisions.choice: the forms that urge: "let us have" and "let us serve"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ between the forms meaning "let us have" and "we have", and between "let us serve" and "we serve"; the pairs sounded alike when read aloud. The SBLGNT reads ἔχωμεν and λατρεύωμεν. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a kingdom that cannot be shaken: what remains after the final shaking of verse 27
decisions.reason: The readers are already receiving it. Compare Daniel 7:18, where the holy ones of the Most High receive the kingdom and possess it for ever.

decisions.choice: serve: worship God with the service of a priest
decisions.reason: λατρεύωμεν is the word for the service of worship in the tabernacle (8:5; 9:9; 10:2; 13:10). Now all God's people serve him in this way (9:14).

decisions.choice: our God is a consuming fire: Deuteronomy 4:24 (also 9:3)
decisions.reason: Moses warns Israel against idols: "the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God" (the Hebrew has the divine name YHWH). The author says "our God". The fire that blazed on Sinai (verse 18) is God's holiness itself, which judges what is false (10:27).

decisions.choice: with deep respect and awe (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer word for reverence.

decisions.choice: un fuego que consume
decisions.reason: A relative clause is plain modern Spanish and says the same as the adjective; it is the picture of Deuteronomy 4:24 (m5). Readable spells out what consuming means.
